chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhraz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Debts are of three types: A man who has a debt owed to him, so he grants respite; and when he has a debt owed to him, he gives it and does not delay, so that is for him and not against him. And a man who, when he has a debt owed to him, demands full payment; and when he has a debt owed to him, he pays it in full, so that is neither for him nor against him. And a man who, when he has a debt owed to him, demands full payment; and when he has a debt owed to him, he delays payment, so that is against him and not for him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of debtors and creditors in Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi categorizes debtors and creditors into three ethical archetypes, highlighting the superior virtue of the one who combines leniency in collecting debts with promptness in repaying them. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle of 'Ihsan' (excellence) in financial transactions, where being 'for oneself' implies gaining spiritual and social merit, while being 'against oneself' denotes loss of status. The text underscores the moral weight of delay ('tatil') in repayment, a key concept in Islamic commercial ethics.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Muhraz, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The debts are three – A man has (a debt) for him, so he repites, and when it was against him, so he gives it and does not overlook it, so that is for him and not against him; and a man when there was (a debt) for him he wants it fulfilled, and when it was against him so he fulfils it, so that is neither for him nor against him; and a man when there was (a debt) for him so he wants it fulfilled, and when it was against him he overlooks it, so that is against him and is not for him’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Khalaf ibn Flammad from Muhriz from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

Debts are three. One man is he who when a lender gives the borrower respite and the borrower pays it off without delay. In his case it is all for him and it is not against him. There also is a man who as lender asks for payment and as a borrower he pays in time. In his case there is nothing for or against him. There is a man who as a lender demands payment and he as a borrower delays payment. In his case it is against him but not for him.”
